findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.chainhelix.io" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: bridge_flows, instrument_state · Private data: proof_spec, list_reveals, daily_digest, data_changelog, attest, webhook_register, stream_register, stream_register_all, standing_watch, webhook_status, webhook_unregister, latest_signals, verified_agents, whale_flows, buy_key, key_order_status, claim_key, stablecoin_flows, liquidations, bridge_flows, wallet_risk, agent_report, hire_plan_rebalancer, hire_plan_gridtrader, hire_plan_yieldopt, hire_plan_healthmon, verified_delivery, delivery_status, screened_payer, cleared_buyer, buyer_clearance, instrument_state, verify_instrument_signal, lexicon_resolve, lexicon_bulk, lexicon_statement, lexicon_bundle · Public sink: attest, webhook_register, webhook_status, webhook_unregister, session_stats, hire_quote, hire_plan_rebalancer, hire_plan_gridtrader, hire_plan_yieldopt, hire_plan_healthmon, verified_delivery, delivery_status, screened_payer, buyer_clearance, instruments, lead_alert_spec · Destructive: webhook_unregister, hire_plan_healthmon.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
